basics.name: DMG-Lib (Digital Mechanism and Gear Library / Digitale Mechanismen- und Getriebebibliothek)
basics.url: https://www.dmg-lib.org/ (redirects to the portal at https://www.dmg-lib.org/dmglib/main/portal.jsp; English interface via ?context_setLangCode=en)
basics.resource_type: digital library (with a mechanism catalogue, a searchable mechanism database, interactive animations, videos, CAx files, a multilingual thesaurus and full-text historic and modern literature)
basics.license: All rights reserved. The Conditions of Use (section 5) say the content is protected by copyright, may be copied only for private, non-commercial use (German Copyright Act section 53), downloads get a one-time, non-transferable licence, and any commercial use is forbidden. Section 6 says the website may not be copied, republished or redistributed without DMG-Lib's consent. What this means for the encyclopedia: link to DMG-Lib pages freely, but do not copy its images, animations or text into the encyclopedia without permission
basics.language: Mixed. The interface is available in German, English, Spanish, French, Italian and Romanian. Content is mostly German (e.g. 'Malteserkreuzgetriebe', 'Schrittgetriebe'), with a large English set (the Artobolevskij mechanisms, which give English, French and Russian names) and some French-only entries
basics.year: Project funded 2004-2009 by the German Research Foundation (DFG, LIS programme), then extended in the EU thinkMOTION project 2010-2013, which also fed its content into Europeana. Since then it has been kept running by the non-profit association DMG-Lib e.V. in Ilmenau. The newest dated content seen on the portal is a 2016 obituary on the home page and an events list running to 2018, so the site looks largely unchanged since about 2018 [uncertain]
basics.access_barrier: none (no login needed to browse, search, view animations or play videos)
basics.image_license: Same as the text: copyrighted, private non-commercial use only, per the Conditions of Use. Many images are scans of historic books and 19th-century models, which may themselves be public domain, but DMG-Lib does not mark them as such. Items are also listed on Europeana (each item page links to its Europeana record), but the rights statement on Europeana could not be checked because europeana.eu is blocked here [uncertain]
basics.authority_level: academic (a university research project led by TU Ilmenau with TU Dresden and RWTH Aachen, now run by the DMG-Lib e.V. association and linked to IFToMM Germany. Content comes from university model collections and published literature, but individual entries are not peer-reviewed)

coverage.covers: Mechanisms and gears (mechanism and machine science) as a whole: linkages, cams, gear trains, friction drives, wedge, screw, belt and chain drives, hydraulic/pneumatic mechanisms and step (intermittent) mechanisms, plus the literature and people behind them. The home page counts are: 3,114 mechanism descriptions (functional models and machines), 36,078 documents (31,862 in full text), 2,818 interactive animations, 3,465 videos, 1,905 CAx files, 45,829 images, 5,823 people, 1,784 thesaurus concepts and 28 software tools. The mechanism descriptions include physical teaching models from TU Dresden (452), RWTH Aachen (328), TU Chemnitz (214), TU Ilmenau (174), Leibniz Universitat Hannover (52) and IFMA Clermont-Ferrand (386), plus 909 entries from Artobolevskij's collection of over 4,700 mechanisms (short entries grouped as 'Clutch and coupling mechanisms', 'Indexing mechanisms' and so on), and Reuleaux models
coverage.organisation: Several routes: (1) browse the mechanism descriptions by 'fundamental mechanism' type (Reuleaux's groups), by application area or by the collection where the physical model is held; (2) an A-Z list of all 3,114 mechanisms; (3) a 'Mechanism search' form with facet filters (function, planar/spherical/spatial, number of links, input and output motion, degrees of freedom, relative position of input and output shafts, fundamental type, revolvability); (4) a free-text advanced search; (5) separate browsing of literature, animations, videos, CAx files, images, thesaurus and people; and (6) a timeline. For a beginner who doesn't know the terms it works poorly: titles are often German terms (e.g. 'Schrittgetriebe, stufenlos verstellbares') and the filters use engineering vocabulary ('transfer function', 'guidance mechanism'). The A-Z list mixes German, English and French titles, so the same type shows up under several names
coverage.scope_match: high. It is a very large catalogue of mechanism TYPES rather than hardware, and includes many of the project's special behaviours (ratchets, overrunning clutches, safety friction clutches, ball-click detents, locking levers, toggle linkages, self-locking gears, Geneva drives, harmonic and cycloidal drives, differentials). It is aimed at engineers and historians, though, and has almost nothing on 3D printing, powered connectors or adhesives
coverage.taxonomy_used: Reuleaux-based 'fundamental mechanisms' with 9 top-level groups (counts from the browse page): link-containing mechanism (linkages, 2,275), cam mechanism (202), gear train mechanism (364), friction-based mechanism (39), wedge mechanism (11), screw-containing mechanism (53), belt and chain drives (38), mechanisms containing a pressurising medium (46) and step mechanism (intermittent motion, 99). A mechanism can sit in more than one group. There are also 8 application areas (production, living/leisure, transportation, agriculture, medical technology, academic, several, other) and a function facet (function mechanism, guidance mechanism, summation mechanism, differential mechanism, adjustable mechanism, locking mechanism). The Artobolevskij entries also carry his own group names (e.g. 'Clutch and coupling mechanisms', 'Indexing mechanisms'). A separate page lists the Voigt catalogue of Reuleaux models (classes A-Z, e.g. N 'Sperr- und Schaltwerke' = ratchets and indexing, O planetary gear trains, P articulated couplings, X clock escapements, Z couplings)
coverage.example_types: Safety friction clutch (torque-limiting clutch); Ball-type overrunning clutch (freewheel); Ratchet clutch with face engagement; Lever-type stop with a reversible pawl (reversible ratchet); Ball-click index / Spring-type indexing device (detent); Ratchet-type stop with a flexible link; Four-bar locking lever mechanism; Lever and spring latch; Lever-type eccentric-cam clamp (cam lock); Toggle linkage (over-centre); self-locking gear; Malteserkreuzgetriebe (Geneva drive, internal and external); Harmonic Drive / Wellgetriebe (strain-wave gear); Planetengetriebe, Cyclo- (cycloidal drive); Quaife limited slip differential; Differential bevel gears with limited automatic locking; Oldham coupling (Oldham-Kupplung); Double Hooke's joint (double universal joint); Scotch yoke mechanism; Torpedo-Freilaufnabe mit Rucktrittbremse (coaster-brake freewheel hub); Cone-wedge coupling; Worm gear; Solenoid
coverage.making_methods: General mechanical engineering, machine design and the history of machines. There is nothing on 3D printing, CNC, woodwork or maker processes
coverage.item_count: 3,114 mechanism descriptions; 2,818 interactive animations; 3,465 videos; 1,905 CAx files; 45,829 images; 36,078 documents (31,862 in full text); 1,784 thesaurus concepts (counts shown on the portal, September 2026)
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: torque-limiting: yes (e.g. 'Safety friction clutch', 'Lever-type friction clutch'); self-locking: yes ('self-locking gear', wedge-type stops and clamps); hand-release only: partly (locking levers, spring latches, lever-type locks); one-way/ratchet: yes, many (ratchet clutches, overrunning clutches, pawl stops, freewheel hub); indexing/detent: yes (ball-click indexes, spring-type indexing devices, Geneva and step mechanisms); over-centre: yes ('Toggle linkage', toggle clamps); compliant: a few (ratchet stops with flexible or elastic links, spring links) but no compliant-mechanism section; print-in-place: no; gear trains/gearboxes: yes, strongly (364 gear-train entries including planetary, harmonic, cycloidal, worm and differentials); powered connectors: almost none (a 'Solenoid' and a 'Magnetic stirrer' entry, and no electromagnetic latches); adhesive types: no
coverage.entry_structure: Name (often in 2-3 languages); a thumbnail image or drawing; a short function description; a structured data table (planar/spatial, number of links, drive and output motion, degrees of freedom, fundamental mechanism type, number of inputs and outputs, whether it can fully rotate, relative position of the shafts, transfer function such as 'dwell' or 'oscillating'); application area; the collection it belongs to; where the physical model is held, who made it, when, materials and size; links to videos, interactive animations and images; permanent links to DMG-Lib and Europeana. The Artobolevskij entries are shorter: a name, a line drawing, the collection group and a note of its number in Artobolevskij's book. There are no design rules and no how-to
coverage.audience_level: undergraduate / professional / research (lecturers, students, design engineers and historians, as the project page says)

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: low. It is heavy on jargon and multilingual (many titles only in German), the filters use academic mechanism-theory terms, and there are no plain-English explanations. Its saving grace is the large number of videos and interactive animations, which show the motion without needing words
usefulness.has_images: yes. 45,829 images: photos of physical teaching models (acrylic display-case models, 19th-century metal and wood Reuleaux models), line drawings from Artobolevskij, and scanned book figures. Quality ranges from good model photos to small, low-resolution thumbnails and scans
usefulness.has_animations: yes. 2,818 interactive animations play in an in-browser HTML5 'AIS5' player (drag with the mouse to step through the motion), many of them made from figures in historic books. There are also 3,465 short videos of physical models (MP4/WebM, often very small, e.g. 240x344 pixels) and WebGL, VRML and Cinderella interactive models
usefulness.gaps: No plain-English explanations or 'what is this good for' guidance; many entries are German-only; no design rules (clearances, torque, strain) and no 3D-printing or maker advice; no downloadable STL/STEP files for making parts; almost nothing on powered connectors, snap fits, compliant or print-in-place joints, everyday quick-release hardware or adhesives; duplicate entries under different language names; a dated JSP-based interface with results pages that need a browser session; and a strict reuse licence
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: yes. Every mechanism, animation, video and image has a permanent link in the form handler?mcdsc=<id> (and manim=, video=, image=), which redirects to the viewer page, e.g. https://www.dmg-lib.org/dmglib/handler?mcdsc=3847025 (Safety friction clutch) or https://www.dmg-lib.org/dmglib/handler?mcdsc=1899025 (Wellgetriebe / Harmonic Drive). Linking by type works best for the English Artobolevskij entries
usefulness.reusable_data: Scrape-only on DMG-Lib itself: no public API, dataset download or export was found, and section 6 of the Conditions of Use forbids copying or republishing the site without consent. The list of names could be reused as a reference only with permission. The metadata was aggregated into Europeana through thinkMOTION (each item links to a europeana.eu record), and Europeana's API might offer the metadata under an open licence, but this could not be checked [uncertain]
usefulness.maintained: Online and working (checked September 2026): browsing, the permanent links, the HTML5 animation player and MP4/WebM videos all work. But the content and news look frozen (latest dated items 2016-2018, and a stale 2011 maintenance notice is still in the page code), so it is best treated as a stable archive kept by the DMG-Lib e.V. association rather than an actively growing library [uncertain]
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) Faceted 'mechanism search' by input motion -> output motion (rotation, straight-line, oscillating, screw), degrees of freedom and shaft arrangement (parallel, coaxial, crossing): a good model for the flow chart's 'what motion do you have / need' questions, reworded in plain English. (2) A function facet that includes 'locking mechanism' and 'adjustable mechanism', matching the project's special behaviours. (3) One permanent ID per type, with every media file (video, animation, CAD, images) cross-linked to it. (4) A multilingual thesaurus of terms with aliases, i.e. a proper-name-plus-aliases field. (5) Scrub-through animations (drag to move the mechanism) as a very beginner-friendly way to show how a type moves. (6) Grouping entries by Reuleaux's fundamental types (link, cam, gear, friction, wedge, screw, belt/chain, fluid, step) as a secondary 'family' axis
usefulness.design_rules_given: No. The mechanism entries are descriptive (structure and motion data only). Some of the hosted full-text literature (gear catalogues, textbooks) may contain design numbers, but they are not pulled out into the entries
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: No geometry generator. It lists 28 mechanism software tools (a catalogue of external special and universal mechanism software, CAD add-ons and so on) but does not generate custom parts
usefulness.file_formats: Images (JPG/PNG); videos (original AVI plus MP4 H.264 and WebM); interactive animations (AIS files played in an HTML5 player); CAx files including WebGL, VRML and Cinderella (interactive geometry) models; scanned books and papers (full-text page viewer). No STL or STEP files were seen
usefulness.terminology_value: high for German and multilingual terms: a 1,784-concept multilingual thesaurus of mechanism and machine science, and Artobolevskij entries giving English, French and Russian names side by side (e.g. 'Ball-click stop' = 'Verrouillage par bille'). Good for finding the proper German/English name and translations of a mechanism type, but not for plain-English beginner names
usefulness.decision_support: A faceted 'Mechanism search' form (not a flow chart): pick any combination of function (including locking and adjustable), dimension, number of links, input motion, output motion, degrees of freedom, relative position of input and output, fundamental type, number of inputs and outputs, and revolvability, and it returns matching mechanisms. There is also an 'interactive mechanism search'. There are no comparison tables and no selection advice
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: Built from university teaching-model collections (Dresden, Aachen, Chemnitz, Ilmenau, Hannover, IFMA Clermont-Ferrand), Artobolevskij's 'Mechanisms in Modern Engineering Design' (over 4,700 mechanisms), Voigt's catalogue of Reuleaux models, and digitised books (e.g. Volmer's 'Getriebetechnik: Grundlagen'). It overlaps KMODDL (Cornell's Reuleaux models, which DMG-Lib links to on its 'Mechanisms worldwide' page) and 507/1800 Mechanical Movements-style collections. The thinkMOTION content is republished on Europeana. To cite an original, cite Artobolevskij or the model collection rather than DMG-Lib where possible
